utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Did you have a good rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Waespi: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Boering, yesterday you had said that you had an initial meeting in January 1995 with various people, including General Zivanovic whom you had said that he was the command of the Drina Corps. Now, do you recall whether he was present at the Hotel Fontana meeting, any of those, on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was not present. General Krstic was present. And General Mladic introduced him as the commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think I asked you that yesterday. Do you recall which of the two meetings on the 11th of July Mr. Krstic was present?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the second meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning to the issue we had left off last night, the third meeting Hotel Fontana on the 12th of July, 1995. Now, I'd like you and the others present in the courtroom to see a clip which again was already shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether we see it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see anything yet. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, if we could start again from the beginning. Thank you, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could stop at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the people you have seen so far, can you tell us a little bit who they were.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The three people stepping out of the Mercedes Benz in civilian clothes, I was the driver. They were the three representatives of the Muslim population. They were Mandzic, the other was Camila Osmanovic, and I don't recall the name of the third man, but that was the father of an interpreter. And I also noticed the interpreter Petar in civilian clothes. At the entrance you can see Mladic's bodyguard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now we have another clip, video, from that meeting, if that could be shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall this scene?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us who these people are as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from left to right, in civilian clothes you see Mandzic, the father of an interpreter, Camila, myself, and at the head of the table is seated Colonel Jankovic. The next person is somebody I do not know, next to him. Across is a man in civilian clothes, and he was designated for screening operations, particularly for Muslim men ages 14 to 60 or 70. And the man with the moustache in between them appears to be Colonel Kosovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the next still could be shown.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There you see General Mladic as well as somebody wearing a white shirt who was also involved in inspecting the staff, screening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "screening," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic indicated that if men were found among the population, that they needed to be inspected for their conduct in the warfare, as to whether they had perpetrated war crimes. And this man in the white shirt served this purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did General Mladic indicate the age range of the people who needed to be screened?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 16 to 60 or 65 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall other issues which were discussed at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially with respect to removal of staff, the idea was that the fuel would need to be supplied by DutchBat if it could not be supplied through vehicles. And the sequence of removal of staff, Muslims, first the injured, then the elderly, then the more healthy individuals. As well as a certain security for the DutchBat vehicles, there was personnel to secure them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Major Boering. Now, over the weekend when you were in the Office of the Prosecutor, you have been shown a transcript of about six, seven pages of this video which carried the scenes of this third Fontana meeting. Now, do you recall that you have read in this transcript General Mladic's comment about screening war criminals?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic indicated there that it needed to happen and that once it had happened, the staff would be returned to the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the comment you just made, were these comments contained in that transcript you have read? Or you don't recall.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time, I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a few people who were present at this meeting, and you have seen the people who had entered that Hotel Fontana, getting out of the car. From DutchBat, who was present apart from you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Karremans was also present at that meeting, or rather Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Boering. Now, what did you do after the meeting finished? And perhaps you could start with telling us at what time you recall the end of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting started around 11.00, and ended around noon -- excuse me, around 12.00. We drove back to our compound at Potocari, spoke briefly with Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans about commitments or the contents of the discussion. At any rate, there was some misunderstanding as to whether or not personnel would be evacuated as well as commitments about fuel, commitments by Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans, and that's why I returned to check matters again. I drove back to Fontana and contacted Nikolic and the Commander Kosovic again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they doing when you met them?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said they were having lunch, but they were clearly in the midst of planning operations. They were irritated that I had returned and made it very clear that they had made their commitments and that transports had already been arranged. They urged me to depart quickly because I had no business being there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was somebody else with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only a driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kosovic and Nikolic indicate to you a time when the transports would be initiated?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be in the course of the day, considerably later. But upon the drive back toward the enclave, it was clear when we overtook a convoy that the operations had already begun. And both Kosovic and Nikolic were already in vehicles headed in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many vehicles were part of that convoy which you said you overtook on your way from Bratunac to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of vehicles would those be?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were buses for public transport; others were lorries with -- covered by cloths for normal transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did you arrive in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was around 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was the situation as it appeared to you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance to our compound, General Mladic was busily convincing the personnel, the Muslims, that they would need to be evacuated, and there were camera crews to record the scenes. It was not as agreed, first the injured and the elderly. They were clearly trying to get people into the vehicles quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how many people did you see at Potocari? Can you give a rough estimate?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the vehicles, it was thousands, two or three thousand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these people, were these women, children, men?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a combination of people. Most were women and children, but there were also some boys and occasionally there was a man among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened to the men?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men were selected and gathered in a building across from the compound. I watched that taking place. Then I went to the building to check things out there. And the elite troops of the VRS were present there. They had several dogs to guard or screen. I briefly entered the building. I saw some passports and things and clothes on the ground there. And then I was hastily removed from the building. There were dogs and there were also machine-guns pointed at me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually see these men, the Muslim men? Did you look into their faces?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw a few of them. I looked at them. But there was no interpreter, so I couldn't really contact them through speaking. But I could see clearly that they were very frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the age group of these men you just described?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 12 to 80 or so. It's difficult to guess the ages when people look like they're in such bad shape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at that time, did you make a connection between the comment you just made about General Mladic's words during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I reported this to Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans as well. He was still at his command post, and then he left his command post to check the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a clarification: You said that the General Mladic made a comment about the screening of war criminals between 16 and 60. And you told us that today. And now, a few hours later, you saw, in fact, men of that age group. Now, at that time, did you make a connection that these two events could be linked or not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was any connection, it certainly wasn't a standard interrogation since there were some elite troops standing ready outside the building, a possible execution battalion, a possible execution squad that were ready to march people off behind the building. And there was no opportunity to walk past. There were obstacles. You couldn't pass because there were dogs there and there were soldiers who wouldn't allow you to pass. And we heard some shooting behind the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you had reported that to your superior. Did you do something else to ascertain what happened in that building?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: To ask the UNMOs on site to stay at the building. At any rate, to count how many people were entering. I stayed at the building up to that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what an UNMO is.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military observers from the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many UNMOs were in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It varied. Usually four to six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall the name of this UNMO whom you had contacted at that time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the name was Kingori. The other UNMO in the neighbourhood was de Haan, who was Dutch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said these men were led to a house. In relation to the entry of the Potocari UN Compound, how far away was that house?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was visible, about three or four hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at what time were the buses leaving?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I rode along on one of the vehicles with a coworker of mine to see what would happen. And Colonel Kosovic, who escorted the transport authorised this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what car did you accompany the convoy?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Mercedes Benz belonging to our own battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of you accompanying this convoy?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, to be a witness to what happened to this convoy and to be able to report it in any way possible. It was unclear to me what was going to happen. And it had not been communicated clearly by the Serbs either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the issue of escorts of these convoys discussed before?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this had been discussed at the third meeting with General Mladic because one man from our battalion would be present per vehicle. It was not the case. I was the only vehicle for the entire convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of how many vehicles did this convoy consist of?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Boering, if you could tell us on the map the route which you took out of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll be happy to do that for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could blow up the sort of section, come back towards Kladanj to the left. The middle part of it to the left, yes. That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The route we took was from Potocari toward Bratunac. And then in Bratunac, left to Glogova. And ultimately, at the next fork, we took to left to Milici. And then we travelled west toward Vlasenica, and then we headed toward Tisca. And about there, the convoy stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Major Boering, on the way, what did you see, did you observe, between Potocari and Tisca?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bratunac, we took a left and headed west. And along the way after a few kilometres, the convoy was stopped. And the police escorting us, they were very nervous. We had to go under cover because there were outbreak attempts from the enclave. And there was indeed a type of prison vehicle where people were busy loading something. It was difficult to see. And at a certain point, that operation ended, and the vehicle headed off toward Bratunac. And we were authorised to continue on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that around Tisca, the convoy stopped. Why did you stop there?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped there. It was made clear we encountered Major Sarkic, who I knew from the past. He explained to me that from that point onward, we would need to walk about 6 or 7 kilometres through no-man's-land to escort the population toward Luke Kladanj. And the route was not entirely safe. It needed to be demined first. And after a brief wait, I was invited to come along with the first population group because it was too dangerous for the Serbs themselves to cross no-man's-land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you had met Major Sarkic before. Can you tell us when that was and what his function was or is.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was upon the transfer of DutchBat II to III in early January. And at that point, he was presented -- introduced by General Zivanovic as the contact from the Milici Brigade. So he was our contact if there were any problems or operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did Major Sarkic tell you under which orders he was acting?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he mentioned that. He indicated that he took his orders directly from the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the men who were part of your convoy join you to walk towards the free territory?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, they performed a selection to see whether there were any men left among them. They were removed and taken off to the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were taken off by whom?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: By VRS troops. We couldn't see where they were going. There was no way that they would have allowed us to do that. They would have threatened us with armed force, would have told us we had no business there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time in the day was that when you had met Major Sarkic?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was around 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same day you had left Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, between 5.00 and 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the way between Potocari and Tisca, did you see any people wearing UN uniforms or parts of uniforms or helmets?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly parts of DutchBat uniforms, and you could see those between -- you could see those among the Serb troops, a few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying that these DutchBat uniforms at that time were not worn by Dutch people or people under the authority of DutchBat, but by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were worn by the VRS soldiers. You could tell by the people in charge and their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how come the VRS got hold of these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly through the hostagings of our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the reason why the VRS was wearing or members of the VRS were wearing these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was possible to cultivate trust so that this would indicate to the Muslim population fleeing that they were safe, and then they could surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, to finish, I would like to show you a brief clip again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could comment on what you're seeing.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is at the end of the route that we walked. On the right is -- you see a BH soldier. They walked toward us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you please go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we shall freeze it at one point so you can identify the people on it. But you can continue to explain, Major Boering.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last section through the no-man's-land, and we were met there by the BH soldiers. They disarmed us and took us off as virtual prisoners of war for interrogation. In the centre, you see me and my colleague to the right is Voorman, and to the left is a BH soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that after you arrived in the Muslim territory, you did not go back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually return to Holland?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next, I travelled back to Germany via Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Is it still Major?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I go into your background, I just wanted to get one thing clear. This wasn't the first time that you had seen folks that were not part of DutchBat in UN uniforms. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not really in a war area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you testified in the previous trial, did you not, during the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I acted as a witness in the Krstic trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that trial, you were read, and later on you were shown, a document from the Dutch Institute whereby in that report, it notes, and it's marked as Defence Exhibit 1 in that particular case, that "Soldiers of the BH army fully dressed with blue helmets or blue caps have arrived to the area within 15 metres of one of the observation posts acting as UN personnel. They opened fire from this position into the direction of the position of the VRS. Therefore, it seemed as if the United Nations had opened fire. In this way, they attempted to provoke the fire of the VRS on the observation post, and by doing so, embroil the Dutch Battalion into combat activities." Now, do you recall being shown and being read that report that was prepared by the Dutch Institute?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the previous trial, and also that your colleague Hansel came up with this text, and that it was unclear at the time what the status of this paper was. And I myself have no information about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you did indicate during that trial that there were complaints by Major Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: There have been complaints from Major Nikolic, that's true. But when you say about the specific case you're referring to, I cannot recall that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you're not challenging today that report from the Dutch Institute, are you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm witnessing about what I've seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly, all right. So you're not saying that it is, in fact, false that, in fact, the Dutch Institute would present and prepare a false document noting that Muslim soldiers where you were supposed to be in a demilitarised area protected by DutchBat were, in fact, impersonating themselves as DutchBat firing onto the VRS in order to provoke an incident so that the UN forces, the DutchBat forces, would get involved?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not endorse this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as I listened to your background yesterday, you indicated that you went to a military academy. So I take it the military is your career.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And back then, in 1995, you're a major, and today in 2003 you still hold that rank as major. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yesterday, there was an indication you were a G3. Not being a military man, maybe you can explain that to us, what that means.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous function, I was responsible for operations and trainings in an artillery unit. And that is how I went to Kosovo. And during the period six years before, that I was part of a brigade staff. And on this brigade staff, I was in the G3 section, trainings and exercise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's what that refers to.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And if I get -- if I have it right, you are an artillery man. That's what your specialty is.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you went to Srebrenica as part of the DutchBat unit, and I understand that you arrived sometime in January 1995.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it, when you got there, there was sort of an eight-hour welcoming, you know, welcoming you folks and sort of saying good-bye to the folks that were leaving, and that was prepared by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Bratunac, the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, it took place at the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's when you met for the first time General Zivanovic who had introduced himself, and indeed, from reading your testimony, had even made an impression on you as a soldier's soldier. He introduced himself as the head of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was some other officers, including Major Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would over the period of six months become quite acquainted with Major Nikolic in your capacity as liaison between the DutchBat and the VRS.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, if I have it right, you had weekly meetings -- at least weekly meetings. I believe they were on Tuesdays. Mondays was reserved for the Muslims; Tuesdays for the Serbs; Wednesday was for the civilians in Srebrenica; and then Thursday, Friday for observation. I take it Saturday, Sunday was for rest?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the schedule, but when times of tension arose, then quite regularly, we had no contact with Major Nikolic for several weeks, even though we wanted to have contact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. And there were sometimes, there were sometimes, at least a couple that I can glean from the testimony, where there were some surprise meetings would be invited, and all of a sudden Nikolic and maybe a guest would arrive with Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now since we're on Mr. Nikolic, we'll stay on this topic if that's okay with you, Major, and then we'll get back to your mission. It was your understanding at the time, in your capacity as the liaison officer, and might I say in that capacity you acted more or less as the eyes and ears for the colonel or the lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It sounds to me from reading it, and again I'm not a military man, it sounds to me you were acting more or less like a security intelligence officer, in that capacity. I mean, you're liaisoning, but you're also trying to get information at the same time. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course one gathers information, but my duty, as for duties regarding security and intelligence, that was certainly not the main thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I agree with you on that one. And as I understand it correctly, you reported directly to the lieutenant-colonel. In other words, you had almost like a, for lack of a better term, a separate chain of command. That's who you worked for. Right? And you were charge for the civic aspect, and as I understand it, there was an individual that was responsible for the military aspect, and then you had the major sergeant or sergeant-major, one of those two.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sergeant-major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the sergeant-major was sort of in between, kind of assisting both of you. That was initially?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, originally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then at some point, due to attrition, you know, one of them had left. That's what I mean by attrition. Basically you and the sergeant-major, the sergeant-major took over both those aspects.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The civil and the -- okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within as well as outside the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, right. And so -- all right, now, let's get back to Major Nikolic. You had been there six months, up until the time of the fall of Srebrenica. And as I read the statements that you gave after the fall of Srebrenica and your testimony, perhaps you hold this opinion today, throughout this period, you thought that Major Nikolic was the assistant commander of the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of Major Nikolic was very unclear. And he didn't want to indicate that. When we addressed him as deputy commander, he was reasonably upset about that. And after that, for a brief while, we had no contact with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You mean he objected to being called that, that was your impression?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not want it to be clear to us what his position was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In fact, you had asked him a couple of times, and on one occasion, he had indicated to you that you were not stupid and that you knew what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Could we say -- I mean I take it you have been around military people. You can judge a character as well as I can, we're lay people. Could we say that Mr. Nikolic had a particular aura about him? You know, he demonstrated an aura of, say, lack of a better term, arrogance?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He made it clear that he was the boss, and he had absolutely no problem keeping us waiting for a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, at times, when you would meet with Major Nikolic, you would have to meet another individual, and he was a colonel, I believe. And that was Colonel Vukotic am I getting it right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. But I didn't deal with him very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in your dealings when they were both together, it was clear to you, was it not, that Major Nikolic was sort of disparagingly addressing and behaving towards Mr. Vukotic or Colonel Vukotic?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you might say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying it, not me.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But there was one individual that when Mr. Nikolic was with, all the airs and the pretensions of being arrogant and being a person of authority were more or less gone. Right? You know who I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was, for example, with Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's a general now. Now, but can you think of another -- do you recall meeting him with Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was during Serb Easter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But as I indicate from reading your reports, when he was in front of Colonel Beara, he was more like a, as they say in that part of the world, wet chicken. Very subservient and very quiet.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the situation was very unsafe at the time. And I was in a no-man's-land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying about your behaviour; I'm saying about Nikolic's behaviour. Nikolic's behaviour in front of Beara. In your reports, it was clear that he was subservient when he was with Colonel Beara. That's what I glean from your testimony and statements.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, on one occasion, you had been invited to a meeting, and there was an ambush.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Nikolic more or less kind of laughed about it.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course when Beara shows up, Nikolic is like a little schoolboy hiding behind the skirts of Colonel Beara. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the impression I got, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me stay with Mr. Nikolic just a little bit longer. I want to fast forward a little bit. And I want to talk about the days on the 11th, 12th, and so on. During the meeting, the first meeting, as I recall, you indicated that Nikolic was there front and centre.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One would think he never saw a camera he didn't like because he seems to be in all the footage?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was quite handy in handling those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, as I understand your testimony from the previous case and from your statements and from -- we touched upon a little bit today here in your direct examination, during the evacuation process, I'll leave it up to the Trial Chamber to determine whether it was a forcible transfer or deportation, so we'll just call it evacuation, if that's okay with you. During that period, you had some extensive dealings, or at least you were able to observe Mr. Nikolic being somewhat -- quite involved in that process along with another gentleman by -- I believe he was Kosovic?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you noticed that they were sort of together, almost glued together, making arrangements with the buses. And in fact, if I understand it correctly, it was quite visible at the time that Nikolic was working side by side along with Kosovic during that process?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the meetings, and if I understand it correctly, you were at all three meetings?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was quite visible to you also that Nikolic was sort of part of that -- at least present during those meetings.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present at the meetings, perhaps there was one where he was briefly absent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And in fact, I believe you noted - I can't recall whether it's in the statement or your testimony - that he left suddenly, and that caught your eye. I take it you're a man of detail.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me -- let's move on to another topic, if that's okay with you. And I want to talk a little bit about the DutchBat mission. First, we're going to go to the general. I know you touched on it a little bit more, if you can bear with me, and then we'll go from there. Okay? Is that all right with you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as I remember yesterday, you indicated that there was -- there were three parts to the mission of DutchBat in Srebrenica during that period.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I had it written here someplace. Let me get it here. One was to secure a safe area.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another one was to demilitarise the enclave.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other one was humanitarian assistance. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now when we say secure a safe area, I take it what you mean by that was to secure the people that are inside the enclave. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, also for going outside, try to prevent it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my next question. See, now you're doing my job. You're anticipating. That's okay. So part of it was to secure inside because you want to protect the people that are inside the enclave, but also secure the people that are outside the enclave because they were being attacked by the military that was within the enclave. Right? Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, there were complaints from Major Nikolic, so that's what we were to take care of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that there were complaints. But certainly, you're not trying to suggest that those complaints were unfounded; certainly you're not saying that?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, exactly. And I just want to make sure that I was clear. Because at least in the Krstic judgement, on paragraph 30 of that judgement, because of testimony taken in that case, they describe an incident that took place about the time that you were there. I was wondering whether you knew anything about that incident, whether it was investigated, and it had to do -- it was a relatively small incident, they burned down a few houses and killed just a few people - they were all Serbs by the way - and this was, I believe, early in the morning of June 26, 1995.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Were you aware of that incident?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I don't remember exactly. But there happened several incidents that made it clear to us that we had this role to play.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. But I take it if we find it in that judgement, that there was testimony with respect to an attack on June 26, which is only, what, two weeks before the attack on Srebrenica, that that incident did, in fact, occur?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the witness just said that he doesn't remember exactly. And second, it's doubtful whether it makes sense to refer to a judgement rather than specific witness statements or parts of testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I understand that the witness did not remember the particular incidents, but he said that there are several incidents that happened around that time. And I see no problem by the Defence counsel using the judgement of another case. You may proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the second aspect of your mission was the demilitarisation of the enclave. Help me out here. Srebrenica was declared an enclave back in, what was it, 1993?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the military structure that existed within the BH, there was light armour present. And somewhat heavier armour had been collected in a weapons collection point and was managed by DutchBat. And in particular, the light armour still present should not have been there; and therefore, we had the duty to try and trace it. And when we got a hold of it, to store it at the weapon collection point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So getting back to what I was trying to suggest, here we are in 1995 when you come in. Srebrenica is declared an enclave under the protection of the UN, and one of the mandates or one of the requirements, I should say, for it being an enclave was that it be demilitarised. So at this point when you arrive and throughout the period that you were there, the enclave was still not demilitarised. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the armour still present, if that is part of the definition, then it was not demilitarised. And I do not mean armour, but light arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But light arms kill, do they not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And soldiers carry light arms, do they not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So from that aspect, soldiers in -- let me back up. Were there soldiers in Srebrenica during that period of time? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And those soldiers had arms. Right? Not heavy arms, but they had arms; right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we saw them carrying arms, then we were supposed to confiscate them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask whether you saw and confiscated. I'm sure you were doing your job. But you're surely not trying to suggest here today that the soldiers that were in the enclave at the time did not have arms.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had arms, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, they had held you hostage for four days.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they held other Dutch soldiers hostages over there at that period; right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but whether these were soldiers or farmers...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, come, come, Major, you were in a particular area, were you not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when -- well, I would like to talk about when you were kidnapped or when you were held hostage, when you were a prisoner of war; right? Or were you AWOL? Do you know what I mean by AWOL?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were, one might say, hostaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- one might say. Were you able to leave at your own free will, or did Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans have to negotiate your release? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not Karremans who had to negotiate; it was Ramic who had to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who's Ramic?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of staff of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which army?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's the one who had to negotiate. Of the army of the soldiers of BH. He was to negotiate with Zulfo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we're going to get to that. We're going to get to that. But I'm a little confused here from your statement, okay. Now, you gave a statement back on 6 May -- I'm sorry, 28 September, 1995. Do you recall that, giving a statement?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead. I have made several statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking if you remember giving the statement. That's all.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made the statement, but specifically on what date and what statement it was...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have a chance to review your statements when you met with the Prosecutor - I don't know how long you were meeting with him - to go over your testimony, but did they show you your statements?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read a number of statements. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did they actually let you have them so you could hold on to them, read them at your leisure, or did they just show them and take them back?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read them properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean -- did they physical let you have them? In other words, do you have your statement with you today?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have my statement with me from the previous trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, but not your statement that you gave, I take it, back on 28 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could, I have enough copies, Your Honour, I hope.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is a statement that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just to make sure, I take it you had an opportunity to read it before. I don't have a signed statement with me. Can I assume or can -- not me, but can the Trial Chamber assume that you read it carefully after it was completed to make sure that it was true, accurate, and complete?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed a Dutch version, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But -- I take it you do read English.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it wouldn't be a problem for you to look at a portion if I were to direct you in the right direction. It would be page 3, and it would be the second-to-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, there's a number on that page, and it's 00443269.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, he said: "I saw Ramic, Naser Oric, and a man I later understood to be Zulfo standing there." We'll get to Zulfo later. "Zulfo told us to stay and join the other Dutch troops." From that, I gather there were other Dutch troops being held hostage, too.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to go there to negotiate for their liberation. And the result was that I could join them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the negotiator of the hostages became a hostage himself.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How many Dutch troops were being held hostage there?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About 10. And these were the folks that were there to make sure that the place was demilitarised?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was by order of the UN that we had to patrol that area in particular, especially for demilitarisation and the freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And so as part of their duty, they went into this area. Do you recall the name of that area?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bandera triangle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was more like the other triangle where ships and planes disappear.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I'm still here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then it says: "We were held there for four days." And by that I take it you were not free to go. You were captive.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I wasn't threatened with armed violence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't say that you were threatened with armed violence, now did I? You can be held hostage without being threatened with armed violence.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. "Eventually Karremans went to talk to Naser Oric, and others came from Tuzla to let us go."

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from this I understand it was Karremans, and that's why I said Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans had to come rescue you. By that I meant he had to go and negotiate with an individual by the name of Naser Oric. And then apparently he had his higher-ups in Tuzla, and then they had to intervene in order for you to be released, you and your colleagues, because you were in an area where the Muslim army within the enclave was operating, and they did not want you or other DutchBats around seeing what they were up to and how heavily militarily they were armed at that location. Is that a fair characterisation?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an area we were not allowed to enter. And it was -- pertained to Zulfo, and whether that was because of the military or smuggling operations, or whatever type of operations, I was never able to ascertain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But when you say, sir, that you were not allowed to enter, that area was part of your mandate, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say you were not allowed --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were allowed to -- we were allowed access to certain areas along the roadside, but we weren't allowed to actually enter the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And I take it when they won't let you in, they don't want you in those areas?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were areas where we were not welcome, and Karremans determined whether or not those areas needed to be patrolled. And I did not always witness what happened in practice over there. Obviously there were patrols in those areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now you say "we were not allowed" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think during the break, the witness can have a chance to read his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. And I can provide him with other statements so that he can be up to speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, I take it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you -- now just one point of clarification, and it was an oversight on my part. When you were held captive as a result of wandering into the region called the Bandera triangle, what period are we talking about, what months if you recall?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just arrived?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the soldiers that were there already that you went to negotiate, had they arrived with you at the same time, in January?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were part of our battalion, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as I understand part of your duty, as we talked about earlier, was to have these meetings. Mondays you would meet with the Muslim military of Srebrenica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a certain sequence, but that's perfectly possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I'm going by what you had testified earlier. But it doesn't matter whether it was Monday or Tuesday; that's not the important part. But what's important is I take it during that period, you would meet with the commander of the military, and here you describe it as "Operational Group 8." And I take it that was Naser Oric. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that Group 8, do you know or are you aware of the fact that it was later renamed the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my memory goes back that far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your report, in fact, you give a little outline of all these individuals. You speak a little bit about Mr. Oric, his chief of staff Ramic. Is that the same Ramic that was injured, by the way, when they were trying to helicopter in, into the enclave?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And just so everybody understands, during that period while you were there, the BiH army was -- the Muslim army was helicoptering in military hardware while at the same time you were trying to keep the hardware out of the enclave. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of our period in the enclave, there was more helicopter activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But that helicopter activity wasn't sort of a mode of transportation, like we would take the bus or the trolley here to go from point A to point B. It was a means of transporting military hardware, perhaps military individuals, soldiers or commanders.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's perfectly possible. I didn't see it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you were aware of it?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was being watched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your capacity as the liaison officer, did you sort of bring it up with Mr. Oric and say "What's happening, commander? You know you're not supposed to have these flights. You know you're not supposed to have all this equipment." Did you bring it up with him in your weekly Monday morning meetings?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically about the helicopter activity at the end of the period, Oric was not in the enclave at that time, but we definitely made clear that that would not be tolerated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was tolerated.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to avoid doing so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my -- I guess my statement is or my question, it was in fact tolerated because DutchBat didn't do anything about the flights, they kept coming in. And isn't it a fact -- and this is a compound question, so why don't I just stop at that. You didn't stop the flights from coming in. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They kept continuing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They kept continuing, right. And would it be fair to say, in fact you've already said it in your previous testimony, that Srebrenica was becoming more militarised during this period than it had been when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, around the last month, the last months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: June, May, June; right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we talked about the incident in June 26 when there was the raid on the Serb village where they killed the Serb villagers there and burned their houses. That was during your watch as a DutchBat in Srebrenica when it was supposed to be demilitarised, and it was in fact getting militarised. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, yesterday you were asked a specific question dealing -- comparing actually the VRS with the Bosnian army, if we could refer to it as an army, which is what you said yesterday. Those were your terms, meaning the BH army. Now, you indicated yesterday that it was your opinion that the Drina Corps was fairly well organised. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you were asked about the Bratunac Brigade. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had a particular opinion about the Bratunac Brigade yesterday, did you not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they were organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, okay. Let me go back to what you stated. I have yesterday's transcript. Okay, and this is on page 67, for the record. It's the unofficial version of the transcript, but I think it will help us here. It says, on line 15, you answer: "The organisation was in fact an organised Drina Corps with clear, rigid system of command. What I saw of the Bratunac Brigade, it was a clear structure with sufficient staff and arms in the sense of artillery and tanks." And then you were asked about making an observation of the BH army, as it was described, and you did so. You indicated that "It was lightly armed, primarily hand firearms and machine-guns and limited other arms." And of course, earlier on the page on line 9 you indicate, as I stated earlier, when asked about the BH army, you stated "To the extent that we could refer to that as an army." So my question to you, sir, is with respect to the Bratunac Brigade. Obviously, you had some contacts with an individual, Mr. Nikolic, Major Nikolic, over a period of six months during which period, or even up until today, you weren't clear what exact function he carried out, other than he was a point of contact with you as being the representative of DutchBat and he being from the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of his exact function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was more than a liaison officer and behaved like a chief of staff or a deputy commander with sufficient mandate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now you never met, and you state this in your statement, in fact. You never met the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during your period as a liaison officer, you would make periodic trips to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to Fontana, the hotel there, with limited freedom of movement. And I used that occasionally to turn off and try to recognise some units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean do some spying while you're there? Observation.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Observation, yeah. Yes, observation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Gathering of evidence. Collecting information.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, the Fontana Hotel is in Bratunac, is it not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, while you were in Bratunac on those many occasions, and from what I read, you visited quite often there, did you ever request to meet with the commander of the Bratunac Brigade? Yes or no. If you can recall.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a request. Whether it was the Bratunac Brigade or the Drina Corps, it was unclear. But after certain incidents, meetings were requested. There was no affirmative response to those requests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never made a request, sir. Isn't it a fact you and Colonel Karremans have a meeting with the commander of the Bratunac Brigade? Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never went to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We weren't allowed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether you were allowed. I'm asking if you went. I'm trying to be precise.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so am I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you make a request, and they said "You're not allowed"?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Nikolic indicated that we were not allowed in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So to the extent that you had any contact with the higher-ups of the Bratunac Brigade, it was through Mr. Nikolic, Major Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And so you don't know today for a fact whether Mr. Nikolic was communicating your wishes, your desires, your expectations, to his commander whom you never met in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And might I add you never met the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not meet him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was never at those crosspoint meetings that you had when Nikolic would show up with Beara?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, and I need you to work with me on this one, help me out here, please, you indicated that -- you know, you gave a description as to the strength and operational capabilities of the Bratunac Brigade. Today, you tell us you had limited access in Bratunac once you got to Bratunac, though you kept a watchful eye. May I ask, may I ask how many tanks did the Bratunac Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know about that is that the enclave was under fire from strong calibre -- high calibre weapons from the mountains, from Bratunac, and that Major Nikolic occasionally stopped by there on patrol, according to what he told me. And whether they were tanks or artillery or tanks firing indirectly, I can't judge that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me get this straight now. I'm a little confused. You drew a conclusion yesterday that the Bratunac Brigade had tanks because in your opinion, expert opinion, might I add, as somebody who is an artillery man, indicated that there was firing coming from the Bratunac area.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from that, you concluded that it must have been or it is, in fact, the case that the firing was done by the Bratunac Brigade, one; and number two, that the Bratunac Brigade had the tanks. Am I correct in making that assumption?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and also based on conversations I had at the observation posts with soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade, I often came there and talked extensively with the soldiers there or who had served there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you get more information that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you weren't just relying on Nikolic; you were going to the soldiers and seeing if you could pry some information out of them.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were waiting for Major Nikolic. He didn't show up. And we waited there, and if you spend an hour or two waiting there...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're trying to pry some information out. That's your job. And I take it these soldiers were telling you that the Bratunac Brigade had tanks. Is that your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They certainly spoke about artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that mean -- can you equate one with the other? I mean, help me out here. I'm not a military man. Are you posing a question to me? Do you want me to rephrase the question?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mm-hmm means yes, I take it.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So when they were saying to you about artillery, you took that to mean automatically, exclusively, axiomatically that that meant tanks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can get into technical details about artillery and tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not trying to get into any technical details because you are far more a superior expert than I am. But here today, or yesterday, you made an observation to this Honourable Trial Chamber that the Bratunac Brigade had tanks. Now today, I'm trying to figure out whether that was just a misunderstanding on your part; in other words, you assumed that since there may have been volleys from tanks coming from the Bratunac area, that those were from the Bratunac Brigade, or whether in fact you know, having seen, observed, or have documentation showing that the Bratunac Brigade did, in fact, have tanks?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Bratunac Brigade area, when the enclave fell, we were on our way to Fontana. In that neighbourhood, there were enough tanks there. Also along the path before that, through information from UNHCR convoy reported to me that tanks were indeed being delivered to the neighbourhood of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, all right. I don't want to seem as if I'm trying to be argumentative, but I'm trying to be specific here. Let's agree that tanks were there, in the area in which you're describing. Can we assume today that the assumption that you are making, because of the location of those tanks, that automatically and exclusively those tanks were from the Bratunac Brigade? Do you know that for a fact?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you don't know that as a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know for a fact how many other units of the VRS were operating in that vicinity? Do you know for a fact?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only based on what was reported to me, but not through my personal inspection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say reported to you, does that mean afterwards? You know, weeks later, months later, or reported to you at that particular period?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, around that point in time, yes. I have a lot of sources of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those sources of information tell you, sir, that those tanks belonged to the Bratunac Brigade? That's what I'm trying to get at.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a specialist in that field, so I cannot give you an affirmative answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said yesterday that the Bratunac Brigade, okay, it was a clear structure with sufficient staff and arms in the sense of artillery and tanks. I'm just trying to figure this one out.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of the Bratunac Brigade, I'm assuming that according to the structure, the Bratunac commander was in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're making an assumption now? Or yesterday, you made the assumption?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, all right. We're moving along, then. So if I can understand you correctly, based on your observation of the Drina Corps, you, then, deduced that obviously, if the Drina Corps is structured, the Bratunac Brigade must be structured in a like manner, organised in a like manner, staffed in a like manner, and have artillery and tanks in a like manner, for a brigade; not for a corps but for a brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you might say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so it's an assumption and not a fact that you can tell us with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my limited perceptions, I cannot judge that 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly, nor could you judge with your limited perceptions - and I don't mean this in a despairingly manner - but whether the troops that were firing in Srebrenica or were engaged in battle at that period were, in fact, from the Bratunac Brigade and not from other units, from the main staff or from the Drina Corps --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please not move away from his microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please. It's a little bit mixed up now for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, all right.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I hear the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With your limited perceptions, could you tell which units belong to -- which soldiers belong to which units at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment the enclave fell, I saw some of the soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade at the observation post that I came to. I saw them operating in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any of them on tanks?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them on tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move on from this section, and we'll go to the BH army, if we could refer to it as an "army" as you've indicated. Can you please give us a rough approximation of how many soldiers were in this particular army in Srebrenica during that period?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my expertise, in the first place. And secondly, that estimate was often -- our battalion tried to make, and let us say that it was a few hundred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So in your opinion, it was only a few hundred, which would mean to me less than a thousand.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say yes, a few hundred, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now would it be less than 500 or more than 500?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never counted them. And let's say a thousand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you were there six months, sir, were you not, and you were having regular meetings with Naser Oric and some of his colleagues?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever ask them, "Tell us how many soldiers you have"?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was Zulfo, the individual you referred to in your report, and the one that kept you hostage, was he a soldier or was he just one of these renegades running around doing as he wished in these enclaves?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Zulfo can be characterised as one who was the boss, fully the boss in a limited area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that area, he would be over Naser Oric. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly in the period when we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Naser Oric was the commander, was he not?
