utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had several meetings with him?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not so often. Perhaps twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps twice. In living in Srebrenica area, did you get an opportunity to form an opinion based on information that you had been gathering regarding the character of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: And likes being a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Was that -- that's the extent of the information that you gathered?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, there is more information about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you what information -- what did you receive about him, how would you characterise him, what was he up to?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone who was difficult to fathom and it was unclear whether he was concerned with military matters only, that money matters were also involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the sense of black marketeering?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Siphoning off the humanitarian aid that was being provided to the residents of Srebrenica so he could sell it on the black market for his own gains?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. During this period, Naser Oric wasn't there; right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: During a specific period at the end, he was no longer there. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were you dealing with with respect to the BH army?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially Ramic, and when he wasn't there, it was Ekrem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the security and intelligence captain. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. I have some documents here I'd like to share with you. And perhaps you can help me out. We received these from the Office of the Prosecution. If you can take a look at that, sir, for a second, I'd appreciate it. And if you can look -- it's pretty short. Just give it a quick look, and then I'll go section by section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, the number on the top is R0050415.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before, sir?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this document. But UNMO does make reports that I have seen from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you indicated that UNMO were the military observers?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were actually present within the enclave, a number of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were there to observe and gather intelligence or information?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, inside as well as outside the enclave. But outside, they were not welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, they weren't really welcomed inside either.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could move around freely there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They can go to the Bandera area freely while DutchBat could not. Is that what you're suggesting?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a little more freedom there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it they were never taken hostage?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, under -- in the first page, at least -- it would be the second page of this, it's dated, as you note, 7 July, 1995. And at the last page, page 5, it's signed by a PHD Wright, MIO, SNE, whatever that stands for. On number 2, it talks about the ABiH corps. Now, says the 2nd Corps. 28th Division was part of the 2nd corps, was it not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it does make a description here. It says: "It is worthy of note that the ABiH within Srebrenica and Zepa, although poorly armed and probably not that much less in number than the total number of infantry in the Drina Corps." "Probably not much less in number." Now, let me ask you, before I ask you whether you agree or disagree with this, the UNMO, are they a reliable bunch? Can we trust their observations?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and their reports, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So they have a certain amount of credibility to be tested, at least, in this trial.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you agree or disagree with this statement: "That the ABiH within Srebrenica and Zepa, although poorly armed are probably not that much less in number than the total number of infantry in the Drina Corps"?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing at all about Zepa. So without getting Zepa involved, and this is a report to Tuzla with information also from outside the enclave concerning other infantry units of the Drina Corps, so I can't say anything at all about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go down to number 6. Maybe you can help us there on that one. It says: "Naser Oric, commander of the 28th division, was reported to be in Tuzla last week and being prevented from returning to the enclave by ABiH" and it gives the following reasons. "A, Oric treats Srebrenica as his personal fief, does not follow the orders of either the government or the army if it conflicts with his personal interests. He is reputed to have made a fortune through his control of the economy and must -- and this must involve dealings with the BSA, that's the VRS, the Serb army. It is, therefore, in the interests -- it is therefore in his interest to keep the enclave quiet." "B, he's an embarrassment of the BiH government, and he is suspected of being a war criminal." Having lived in Srebrenica for six months, having met with Mr. Oric, having been part of that community, having been watchful and observant and engaging in trying to gather information in your capacity as a liaison officer, is this -- what do you think of this? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are possibilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, now I want to take you back -- I'll go through just a little bit more of this. It does talk about the purpose of the attack. And there are two options. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: What paragraph are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to paragraph 10. I apologise. Option 1, conquer Srebrenica enclave; option 2, neutralise Srebrenica enclave. Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it says that option 2 would be more logical choice in military -- for political, military, and personal terms. Okay. Then I want to go to the conclusion, paragraph 18. It says: "ABiH will be happy for enclave to be shelled as it gives media coverage and replaces `Sarajevo, the marred city'. To this end, the 28th Division can expect to be ordered to carry out patrols and provoke the BSA; however, Oric's whereabouts will continue to provide a clue to ABiH policy." What is your opinion of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, this is an unknown conclusion, and I cannot endorse it just like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well I'm not asking you to endorse it, but am I correct to assume from your previous answer that the UNMO had more access to information than you did, and from your own indication, I could rely or we could rely, to some extent, on their reports? In other words, we just cannot outright dismiss their reports.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to show you another report. That was from -- this is from July 9th. The interpreters may want a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was just wondering whether Mr. Karnavas has any copies in B/C/S of this evidence that has been in his possession, I suppose, for a while, or if the Prosecution has B/C/S copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, these documents were disclosed to me as they were disclosed to Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm not arguing about that. I'm just asking if there are any B/C/S copies available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Prosecutor would know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's very unlikely because we are not required to translate these documents into B/C/S, and there are literally tens of thousands of these UN situation reports. So we can certainly check, but it's extremely unlikely that we have it in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, all those documents were disclosed to the Defence team. Right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could take a look at that, and I want to apologise to the French booth. Apparently we did not make enough copies. I want to focus your attention particularly to page 5 and page 6. And for the record, the numbers of the document begin with R0037477 and they end with R0037490. Do you -- have you had a chance to look at it? Would you like some more time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If I could direct your attention to the page 5, the top of it you'll see page 5 of 12.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the bottom it states, it has a number R0037483.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look where it says "military assessment," just read that very quickly, first, second, third, and fourth paragraphs, and then we'll go to the next page. We'll go page by page. When you're ready, let me know.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just for the record, do you know what this document is? Or do you have an idea? Look at the front page; that might help you.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a Sitrep, only I don't know from whom. It's from General Janvier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you characterise it again?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: A situation report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, all right. Okay. A situation report. Now -- and this has, it says on top of it, UNPF. Do you know what that stands for, United Nations Peacekeeping Force?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says HQ, that means headquarter?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zagreb, that's where the headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so this is a UN-generated document?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the page you were referring to is a Sitrep, and at the top it says "From UNPROFOR, internal distribution."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I think it was meant for internal use only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: For G2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I see they used a G3. Is that similar to the G3 you were talking about earlier?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says G2 here, to that's reconnaissance, intelligence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, intelligence. And in your opinion, this was generated by UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Sitrep from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who are UNPROFOR, just so I'm clear on this?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the military boss, so to speak, in all of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was -- and you were --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Croatia. In Yugoslavia, let me put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it the DutchBat were subordinated to them?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were, through a structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, it says military assessment. And it gives an assessment, and it says: "Reduce the size of the enclave in order to be able to free assets for use in other conflict areas, north-east Sarajevo, et cetera, this can be achieved by capturing key terrain along the perimeter of the enclave." That's what it says. That's what they believed at the time; right? And the date is 9 July 1995. And further down, it says: "Eliminate the threat of BiH harassment, patrols, ambushes, from the enclave and increase the control over the enclave." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you flip the next page, that would be page 6, and I'm referring to the third paragraph from the top, it says: "The Bosnian Serbs could halt their advance pending a number of conditions, a complete demilitarisation of the enclave will probably be their highest priority. This would serve the primary goal of freeing troops from around the enclave." All right, so I think here the UN acknowledges that the enclave is not demilitarised, as you've indicated to us from your own observations. And then it says: "The BiH will continue to try to block DutchBat in their OPs," I take it that means operations, "or in positions in front of the BiH. It would involve the use of force, they can colocate within UN positions to use them as human shields. This might provoke a reaction from the BSA with a risk for UN personnel to get caught in crossfire between both factions. The BiH is likely to attempt to capture weapons and vehicles from DutchBat to compensate for their lack of armament." So that was an assessment that was made by your colleagues within the intelligence community of the UN on the ground in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have an opinion with respect to that?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That last part didn't happen. They didn't capture weapons and vehicles from us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But nonetheless, that was a concern.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just give you a fact that it didn't happen. I said it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand it didn't happen. And my retort was, but that was a concern. Right? Something else happened, if I may, you know, move ahead a little bit or jump ahead, and that was the killing of a Dutch soldier by the Muslim army in Srebrenica. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, well, we'll talk about that. But further down, it says, not the next paragraph but the following one: "Similar to what happened in Gorazde, spring 1994, BiH can attempt to draw UNPROFOR, including the RRF, or NATO, into the conflict on BH side. Sudden abandoning of positions along the confrontation line, the simulation of the collapse of the enclave or alarming reports from the Bosnian side on the situation in the enclave will be indicators for this. Stronger involvement of international community could be interpreted by the BSA as an incentive to step up operations and try to eliminate the enclave as well as retaliate against UN forces." Do you have an opinion about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at some point, because of the rules of engagement, it was necessary to ensure that the VRS was actually shooting at the DutchBat, or in order to activate the airstrikes. Is that correct, or am I getting it wrong a little bit? Close air protection, that's what I mean by that.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one of the possibilities of air support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In order to get air support, or close air support, a number of things had to happen. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, Colonel Karremans had promised the army that was in Srebrenica that there would be close air support or airstrikes -- and incidentally, they more or less look the same, don't they, when you're on the ground? When you're on the receiving end?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so from the ground where you were, you had to indicate to your higher-ups that that you're under fire, and therefore you could get the close air support.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was such a relationship.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And in fact, you testified in the previous trial that on one occasion, in order to create a provocation or in order to get the air support, you coordinated with members of the Muslim army to drive up to an area where they would be shot at in order to give the pretext of placing the call to get the airstrikes. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you're referring to is not quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was really an attack within the enclave by Serbian troops, these troops had to be recognised, and their intentions had to be recognised as being aggressive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: And therefore, another verification had to take place, and that's an entirely different word than "provocation".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me rephrase it, then, and correct me if I'm wrong. There were some conditions necessary in order to get air support, right, in order to get NATO, whoever it was, to come over and bomb the positions of the Serbs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If counsel is referring to the transcript of his Krstic testimony, I think it would be fair to show it to the witness, perhaps quote it word by word, since he already said that it wasn't correct what he had put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a reasonable request.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. If I may have a moment. Your Honour, I must apologise for not having an extra copy, but I would be more than happy to share my copy through the usher. It's even underlined. It's convenient for the witness to read, if he could look at it. You may need to flip through the previous page to get the whole context.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still need the transcript?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you have any additional questions about it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do. But let me see if I can get a hold of... In fact, I can get the page -- the relevant page for you. I have it right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra, you want to help?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have an extra copy he can use until our next break if he would like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have it right here, Your Honour. I'm trying to catch my staff unprepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm referring to page 1.156. I don't know if our colleagues from the Prosecution have it handy, but... It says on line 4 that there was a question. It says -- this was a question posed by the Prosecutor to you. I think it was by the Prosecutor. Yes. It says: "So Colonel Karremans guaranteed to the Muslims that there would be close air support. Was there any condition placed on that air support being" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel slow down when reading, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Was there any condition placed on that air support actually being provided to the enclave?" And the answer is: "Would you please repeat the question." Question: "Did Colonel Karremans say that anything had to happen before the air support would be given?" Answer: "Must be clear at that moment that we were, we or the Muslim enclave, should be attacked by Serbs, and there must be a kind of visible contact with them. For that reason, we must first be on the spot." Question: "Did you or any Dutch officer take action to ensure that an actual contact took place between Bosnian Serb army and DutchBat, or Muslims within the enclave?" Answer: "Yes, I did. I contacted military men, the Muslims, and he himself drove, say, into the Serb position. He came back, and he was shot at. His car was shot at. I remember." You were asked: "How did you feel sending the man -- sending the Muslim male in a vehicle to be shot at by the Bosnian Serb army?" And of course, your answer was: "Of course it was not comfortable to do that." "Was he armed at all, this man?" Answer: "When he drove in his car to that position, I didn't see him step into his car and driving, so I don't know." Question: "Now, you say that he was shot at. Did anything actually happen to him? Was he injured?" Answer: "He himself was not injured." So my question to you now that we've refreshed your memory with what you stated under oath at the Krstic trial, you needed to have contact. Right? And so -- and you needed to be on the spot.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we've already indicated that at least -- when we first started I showed you or I read to you a report that came from the Dutch Institute that Muslims dressed in UN uniforms would pose and shoot at -- would pose as DutchBat and shoot at the VRS in order to provoke an attack. In this instance, in essence, you're trying to do the same, are you not? Sending someone to the front line to be shot at so you can look at it, observe it, see that there's contact, so then you can call in to your bosses and say "Send in the planes, strike the VRS forces on the ground." Is that a correct characterisation?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not a correct account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anything that you stated during the Krstic trial that I read from inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you did not do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I know -- well, I tried not to be inaccurate in reading it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the witness was just pausing to explain what he --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, if you want to explain to us, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's very difficult, Your Honour, from this angle. I don't mean to be disrespectful to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to add was that Ramic indicated on several occasions in this case as far as I can remember that he said "Hey, we have been attacked," that the battalion indicated once again there's got to be proof. And that this should be the ultimate proof for air support was one of the reasons for demonstrating that there were troops in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in this instance, the conclusion that I draw from your own words, that you placed yourself in a location and had the Muslim soldier drive up to the line to be shot at. Because later on, you're asked a question by none other than the Prosecution, who I assume briefed you in advance and knew of the incident in order to ask you the question, and they asked you "How did you feel?" Because obviously, as a human being and as a professional soldier, it must have been a very difficult decision for you to ask someone, albeit not a Dutch soldier, but to ask someone to drive up to be shot at so later on you can contact the headquarters and say "There has been contact, and let's get the close air support."

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last part, "let's get close air support" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the part you disagree?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one. And second, did I actually said it's not indicated in the Krstic report because there was indeed one person who was seriously injured and who was transported to the hospital. I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. If we could move on to another area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you are moving to another area, we better take the break right now. But before that, could you indicate how much time are you going to need to finish your cross-examination. It's just with arrangements of the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. I can -- I'm going as fast as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in light of yesterday where I was caught a little bit off guard and not being as diligent as I should have been, I'm trying to be a little more thorough today. I can safely that the gentleman should not check out of his hospital room tonight if he doesn't live in The Hague because I think I'm going to need the rest of the period. It may be a little bit tomorrow, Your Honour, because there were some doors opened by the Prosecution. I'm trying to make it all relevant. And of course, throughout the proceedings, you will see that all of this will be tied in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I just hope you could make the best use of your time. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, I would now like to show you a letter that was provided from Mr. Akashi to Mr. Annan. And if you could take a quick look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, it's numbered R0080307, and it ends with R0080309. It's dated 12 July, 1995. It was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just for clarification purposes, is the Defence proposing those as trial exhibits, Defence exhibits, and I think for ease of reference it would be good to mark them so we can discuss it, perhaps identify, mark them for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a good idea. If the Defence counsel introduces a lot of documents, we better have a mark on them, and then later on it's easy for us to consider whether it should be admitted into evidence or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we also instructed both parties to provide a list of the documents you might use during the direct examination and the cross-examination. Of course, we understand it is a little bit difficult for the Defence to provide us with a list of the documents used in their cross-examination because you could not anticipate what kind of documents you are going to use. But anyway, to facilitate the work, we are expecting that a list of the documents you are going to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I do apologise. Normally, I wouldn't mark it for identification purposes. And again, I apologise. It won't reoccur. The question is where do we go from here for the rest of the day? Do I -- should I just go ahead and then at the end of the day perhaps meet with Madam Registrar here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's a very good idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Again, I apologise to everyone, and I thank the Prosecution for bringing it to my attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look, sir, to the first paragraph, paragraph number 1, again, this is dated July 12th. It says: "Under the circumstances, you may wish to consider the merit of the Secretary-General addressing a letter to the Council which would warn of the dangers of raising unrealistic expectations and remind the Council of those serious issues which he has drawn their attention in the past which events in Srebrenica have again brought into focus." If we flip to the following page, under paragraph number 3, in particular, 3(b), and then 3(c), 3(b) states -- okay, well 3 starts with: "In his report, the Secretary-General has drawn attention to the problems of the safe area regime in the following areas: (b), use of the safe areas by the Bosnian government for military purposes." By that I take it, sir, Major, what they mean is that the Bosnian military, the BiH military or the Muslim military - and I don't mean that in any derogatory sense, but that military that was in Srebrenica - was using the enclave as a staging ground or as a basis from which to launch military operations. I think that's what they're referring to. Would that be a correct assessment of what they mean by this?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: A safe area, a place where they could be as military safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it says "Use the safe areas by the Bosnian government for," for, for, and I underscore "for military purposes."

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you agree with my interpretation, they are using the enclave as a basis as an area from which they can operate, which would mean outside, you know, going outwards, not inwards?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a problem. Draw attention to, it's a problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then "(c), provocation and attacks from within the safe areas." Okay, so in other words, if I understand this correct, Mr. Akashi, and you do know who Mr. Akashi was at the time?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he just for the record?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Akashi was in charge of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the head -- he was the head of the UN mission basically dealing with Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was out of Zagreb; right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where it says "Annan," do you know who we're talking about, which Annan?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's in New York.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it says New York here. Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who might that be?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretary-General.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so then if we go to number 4, it says: "As for the demilitarisation of safe areas, the Secretary-General should remind the Security Council that it took a year following events in Gorazde for the consul to refer to `mutually agreed demilitarisation of the safe areas and their surroundings' in SCR998." I suspect that means Security Council Resolution 998. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me rather difficult English to read. It's difficult to understand, and I don't ordinarily encounter such technical language. No comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if I could then show you something that was generated by UNMO headquarters on July 26th, 1995, maybe it's more in military terms and more akin to what you're used to reading, albeit in English and not Dutch. For the record, the first page has a number on it, R0050422, and the entire package goes all the way through R0050433. I want to direct your attention - I'll walk you through this - first part is paragraph 6 on the first page. It says: "ABiH leadership" --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you tell me the origins and status of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this is a document given to me from the Office of the Prosecution. And this is the manner in which I received it. And it says up here: "UNMO headquarters, SNE." I don't know what that is?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sector North-East maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you would know more so than I would. But at page 6, sir, it seems that our friend that we encountered earlier, PHD Wright, and I take it he's a major, same rank as you, UNMO, MIO, SNE. Okay, so if you could help me out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are having a little bit of trouble following without documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go through the first page. It talks about ABiH leadership. And it says that Oric was a charismatic commander of Srebrenica, and he was not allowed to return by either the BiH government or the 2nd Corps. Then it says: "By reasoning in reference A that's above, it maybe false and it was instead a deliberate attempt to weaken the 28th division. Whatever the reasons, it certainly succeeded in doing so according to UN reports which claim that the local commanders seemed incapable of taking any decisive action." From this, we could gather that Naser Oric was a major component of the 28th Division, as its commander, and that 28th Division was, in fact, operating from within the enclave during the period while you were there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you could read it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read it that way, too? I know I'm reading it this way.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means yes?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could go -- if we could go to the second page, I guess. Now we are at paragraph A, talks about the strength of the BSA. In paragraph B, talks about the strength of the ABiH. And here, their assessment is "Not known, however, the usual estimate of 10 per cent of population would give a force of approximately 4.000. It was not clear before the attack whether all were armed, but it was believed that at least half had SA." What does SA mean? "As well as HMG, LTMOR, anti-tank weapons including RPGs and more modern ones. (Certainly all capable of destroying the tanks against them). There are reports that many of these weapons were thrown away during the march of friendly lines because of the weight." And then it has a comment: "This suggests a collapse of discipline and little control not least because such weapons could have been cached for future use by guerrilla parties." And then the comment ends. Now, would that be a correct assessment based on your six months in Srebrenica, that they had a force of approximately, if the estimate was 10 per cent, 4.000?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not so long ago, I said about 1.000. And if it reads 4.000 here, then that's his estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if I may, and I don't want to dispute with you here, but as I recall, you said in the hundreds. And then wanting to make you a little more precise, I said could it be, you know, less than 500, more than 500. And as I recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the witness clearly answered and said thousand. And he also answered the second question saying that the 4.000 number was the estimate of whoever wrote this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I don't think there's any dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to paragraph 11, paragraph 11 says: "ABiH withdrawal." Okay, are you there?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Rumours of the ABiH fighting their way out began to be reported by 11 July with the final meeting between Ramiz and UN the night before." I take it you're the UN that they're talking about.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ramiz is who, again?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, he was the military leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean he had replaced Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: And when Naser was there, he was chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then it says: "However the town of Srebrenica was only entered that day. For a large body of men from all the over the enclave to start such an operation, the planning and forming up must have started sometime earlier." And then it gives two possibilities. Possibility 1: "ABiH was planning to withdraw long before the situation necessitated it, and it's supported by the seemingly poor resistance put up by the ABiH." And then B, "The breakup was not planned, but rather carried out by small groups resulting in fighting, ambushes in the west and northwest as troops from the east side tried to get through." And then it goes on, and this is something I'm kind of curious, perhaps you can help us out here with: "An interesting footnote to this withdrawal is a well-sourced report from Hakija, chief of police, Oric's henchman, and possible war criminal, escaped with 56 of his men leaving some who volunteered to stay and fight." So from this, can I conclude that the chief of police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Karnavas, may I interrupt you a minute. In the paper you send us, it says "Is a well-sourced report that Hakija," not from Hakija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. "Is a well-sourced report that..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: It's different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because we're talking about Hakija himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "That he escaped with 56 of his men, leaving some who volunteered to stay and fight." And then it goes on: "This seems a large percentage from an approximate total of 120 who, considering they were meant to be keeping law and order." The question I'm asking is was the police in Srebrenica also armed like a military? Or were they merely police officers carrying their usual weapon, if you are aware?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I believe they were allowed to have only very limited arms, and they had to perform their duties as policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever have any contact with this gentleman Hakija?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you had contact with him indirectly?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague was there for the initial contacts. He was also a liaison officer. He did meet with Hakija on a few occasions. And at a certain point, the military police took over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, but he was not military police; he was regular police?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UN, the military police that supervised him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And it says here "Oric's henchman." You know what a henchman is?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could give us your definition of a henchman, so we have at least a standard by which to go by.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody who does somebody else's dirty work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it says "war criminal." So from this could we at least assume that the author of this was led to believe that Hakija, Oric's henchman, was involved in war crimes?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads here "possible".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what I -- yeah. Finally, on paragraph 12, it has the conclusion. And it says: "The advantages militarily seem to have been with the defenders, they at least hold out for rather longer and have inflicted greater losses on the BSA than believed. However, the ABiH leadership seems to have actually acted against their own interests to carry out a successful defence with little coordination, except possibly in withdrawal and no attempt to seize any heavy weapons held by the UN whilst more junior individuals have been allowed to make their own decisions and run." Now, it's this conclusion that I'm rather interested in. Having been there on the ground, you will know perhaps --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. Could I just finish translating this for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in the conclusion, it says "The advantages militarily seem to have been with the defenders..." I take it by "defenders" they mean the ABiH army was in the enclave at the time it was supposed to be demilitarised. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a fairly large force that was inside?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "defenders" here. There's nothing about the size.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. They had the advantage militarily.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had -- the advantage of the terrain when you're defending.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So from that, you cannot conclude that the size, but merely they had a geographical advantage?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the terrain is a very important element there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. And from there, because they had the advantage of the terrain, a smaller force could pin down a much larger force like the Drina Corps. And with the UN protection, can raid Serb villages, burn down Serb houses, kill Serb civilians in order to provoke; and then run back in under the protection of the UN and also have this physical or geographical advantage given the terrain. Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that mentioned here under item 12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't say it was in item 12.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see what you're heading for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me help you out here, then. You've indicated that based on this conclusion, what you can conclude from it that when they say that they had the advantage, the defenders had the advantage, by that, you understand it to mean because of the geographical position, the terrain, a smaller force could, in fact, have an advantage over a larger force. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, so far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so far. So far so good. Now, we add the element of the UN protecting this enclave. And what I am suggesting is that another conclusion could also be drawn, and that is that from this enclave where you have UN protection, a smaller force could use it as a staging ground of going out, committing war crimes, committing atrocities, committing crimes against humanity, and then run in under the safety of the UN flag, and also having the advantage of the physical terrain.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What do I mean by that? Well, what I'm suggesting, sir, is that while you were there, there was a significant -- there was a significant Muslim, Bosnian army presence in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, about a thousand men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's your interpretation, and we have another one that could be as high as 4.000 from here.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you're asking for my interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. But as you indicated earlier, and correct me if I'm wrong as you did earlier, this report was generated by the military observers who had access to information and access to terrain that you did not have. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they had not been into the enclave, those who made this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know this gentleman in particular, so are you discrediting his report entirely, the report that he sent to his superiors?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you what my opinion is about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you differ with his opinion.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned a thousand men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, but we can agree that the physical terrain gave the advantage to those men that were in, whatever the number may be, gave the advantage to them.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I take it if it was an advantage to defend, it must also have been an advantage to go out, commit crimes, provoke, and then run back in under the protection of the terrain, the same terrain that gave them the defensive advantage?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not confirm that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then perhaps you can explain why is it that they were going out repeatedly, committing crimes as late as June 26, 1995, and then running back into the enclave under the protection of the UN flag when this entire area was supposed to be demilitarised as of 1993, and we're talking middle of 1995. What is your explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to me, I already gave you that explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You're not denying the fact that there was a large presence, military presence, in the enclave at that time.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it's your understanding that they just had very few weapons, these folks that were in there, very light?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said they had arms, but no heavy arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No heavy arms.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Particularly tanks and artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to the -- I would like to cover with you as the last part of this area some conclusions that were drawn from the Krstic trial. And I have copies of the paragraphs that I'm going to be referring to. I have an extra copy if you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's enough for the interpreters. We have some extra copies. For the record, I'm referring to the Krstic judgement, and they are paragraphs 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just give it a quick look, sir, and then let us know.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go through it very quickly, paragraph 21, it states that there were between a thousand to 2.000 soldiers from three Drina Corps Brigades were deployed around the enclave. Would that be your estimation?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number, we already discussed. And the units I already indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about -- it says -- this is talking about the VRS.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS with the tanks and the artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it says that "Some extended supports, which you've indicated earlier, that the unit of the ABiH, 28th Division, was not well organised or equipped." It goes on to say: "A firm command structure and communication system was lacking. The Trial Chamber, however, said that it heard evidence that the 28th Division was not as weak as they had been portrayed in some quarters. Certainly, the number of men in the 28th Division outnumbered those in the Drina Corps, and reconnaissance and sabotage activities were carried out on a regular basis against the VRS forces in the area." This would seem to contradict what you indicated yesterday when you described the sizes of the two armies, and in particular, in your remark as you indicated "if we could call it that," that is, the --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depends what you call a soldier. When it's a farmer carrying a weapon or someone in a nice uniform and having a good weapon, that's decisive for how you count them. And I base myself on a thousand, well-armed and well-addressed personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now those --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly another 3.000, if they existed, may have been of the other type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Paragraph 22, I think we all agree it says "Both parties to the conflict violated the safe area agreement." You would agree with that. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at least from within the enclave, there has also been a problem with a possible Serbian attack. But there is no clear evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it says here "both parties" meaning both the Serbian side and the Muslim side. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But today, we have been primarily talking about the Muslim side, you know, and their violating the agreement by maintaining a militarised enclave. Now, in paragraph 23, the Court apparently heard testimony from General Halilovic. Have you ever heard of this individual?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never met him. And my remembrance is not that big, but I think he's one of the leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've heard of him?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he testified, and he indicated that he ordered members of ABiH in Srebrenica to pull all armoured personnel and military equipment out of the newly established demilitarised zone, but that he also ordered that no serviceable weapons or ammunitions be handed over to UNPROFOR. So in other words, if the weapon was operational, it shouldn't be turned over. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's what he testified to.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it from your observations you were able to see serviceable weapons by the Muslim army within the enclave?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as we saw them, we were supposed to seize them. That was our policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: So large quantities of arms of sufficient quality, I have not seen, I have not witnessed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. There was a cache, though, there was a place where they were store weapons, was there not?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. On the compound of the bravo company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those nice and shiny out of the box kind of weapons, or were they more antiques, not serviceable as General Halilovic seems to indicate?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, partially antique, and partially usable. Arms that we seized also went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in paragraph 24, it says that "The Trial Chamber had credible and largely uncontested evidence of a consistent refusal by the Bosnian Muslims to abide by the agreement to demilitarise the safe area." I take it you would not disagree with that conclusion that was reached by the Trial Chamber in the Krstic judgement.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I understand, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And further into the paragraph, it describes the ways they were violating the safe area. Then it goes on to say that "To the Bosnian Serbs, it appeared that Bosnian Muslim forces in Srebrenica were using the safe area as a convenient base from which to launch offensives against the VRS, and that UNPROFOR was failing to take any action to prevent it." This is their conclusion.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it says that it was the conclusion of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the Court concluded that to the Bosnian Serbs, it appeared. Right? This is a finding of fact by the Trial Chamber that at least from their observation it appeared to the Bosnian Serbs, it was a state of mind on the Bosnian Serb side. Right? So I go back to my earlier question to you --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's their opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's their opinion, of course. But it ties into my earlier question when I pointed out the conclusion, and you indicated -- and you corrected me when you indicated that the advantage was with the defenders given the terrain. And then I went on to a very lengthy question indicating that that advantage also applied for offensive purposes as well particularly the UN was there offering safe haven and safe harbour and sanctuary to Muslim fighters by using the enclave as a staging ground to commit crimes outside the enclave.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an interpretation, as it says here, by the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. I want to switch topics, and I want to go to the 11th of July, 1995. If I understand you correctly, yesterday, as well as in some of your previous testimony, and I believe it might be also in your statements, you've indicated that it was the Serb side, the VRS, that had contacted DutchBat requesting a meeting or demanding a meeting?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that your -- do you know that for a fact? Is that an opinion? Is that a supposition, an assumption, a presumption? What exactly is that?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a memory which is present very strongly in my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, does that mean that the memory is correct, or could you be wrong? Because it might be somewhat critical as to who initiated this meeting.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That meeting was requested by -- from the part of the BSA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: BSA meaning the VRS or the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could have some assistance here with the usher. If I could interrupt for a second, I'm only going to be referring to paragraph number 2. And there's another document that I'll give you. It will save us some time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, I've read the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, for the record, the document -- the numbers on the document are R0015489, and R0015490. This document, sir, what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report drafted by Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans, but I have not seen this report. The contents appear familiar, however.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, now who is the letter addressed to, sir?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says to the various officials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says at the top, it says "To force commander"; right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Lieutenant-Colonel Janvier. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've already discussed that he was the commander in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in paragraph number 2, Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans says: "I have been ordered by HQ" that's headquarters, right, "UNPROFOR Sarajevo to enter into local negotiations with BSA forces for immediate cease-fire. It says see appendix. And then it says: "I had two meetings with General Mladic." Now, from this document it would appear that Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans had a conversation apparently with headquarters in Sarajevo, perhaps outside your presence, whereby he was ordered to initiate contact with the VRS in order to enter into negotiations. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be a possible interpretation. Another one might be that we -- that we met. And what I remember is that after the first meeting, Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans requested instructions in Sarajevo as to whether he would be receiving support or had to arrange matters himself. But I'm more inclined to believe the latter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of more matters -- couple of more pieces of evidence on this, on July 18th, there was a letter sent by Mr. Akashi to Justice Goldstone who at the time was the Prosecutor of the ICTY, of the Tribunal here. I'm not so much interested in the letter itself, but in the second page -- and this, by the way, for the record, the numbers are R0050215, and it goes all the way through 218. Now, there's a -- and then you will see the third page is similar to the document that I have just shown you, that is the one that was prepared by Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans. Now, could you look at this particular document, sir, this page 2 --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could look at it, take your time. And please tell us what it is, first, who generated it, and then I'll proceed from there.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could help us out here a little bit. It says, the top part: "HQ, UNPROFOR, Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "Outgoing fax." On the left side, it says: "To: Sector North-East info, Company DutchBat." That would be you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are on the receiving end of this document?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: You get this for your information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, okay. But I guess you're the receiver of this. Can I conclude that, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person supposed to take action is the Sector North-East, and DutchBat is only receiving it for information purposes. That's the military hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for clarifying that. But I guess what I'm -- well, let me go to the right side, then. It says: "From, headquarters, UNPROFOR, acting commander" and I guess there's a correction here, must be a Major-General.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it appears to be Major-General Gobillard. Had you heard of this individual?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not meet him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, but you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he's actually sending this message, and DutchBat at least is getting the information of this?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's sent it to Tuzla, Sector North-East.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And one -- it says in here under paragraph A, although there's a handwritten 1 circled, it says: "Enter into local negotiations with BSA forces for immediate cease-fire. Giving up any weapons and military equipment is not authorised and is not a point of discussion." Now, from that, it seems to appear that what he's suggesting is that someone, DutchBat or the higher-ups in Tuzla are to enter into negotiations, but DutchBat or the UN is not to give up its own weapons. Is that how I am to interpret this?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, they weren't suggesting for the Muslim army not to give up their weapons, but for the DutchBat or the UN forces, peacekeeping forces, not to give up their weapons?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are instructions toward DutchBat. I assume they mean the arms of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So somebody in Sarajevo, this acting commander, that's a pretty high position, don't you think?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's below the commander, I guess the commander is not there, so he's acting as the commander and he's giving the order. And he's not saying, please, maybe, or think about it, this is basically an order for DutchBat to enter into local negotiations with BSA forces. Right?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are instructions to Sector North-East to interpret this, and we receive it for our information. And I remember that Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans telephoned Tuzla about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't remember the true contents from this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The meeting that you had with the folks -- the first meeting took place about what time, sir, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at any rate after this telegram was sent, or at least signed. But I don't remember whether we did it before and/or afterwards. I do remember a phone conversation between Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans and Tuzla as to whether there were actual instructions and what he should observe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But nonetheless, if you look at -- if you look at this piece of document, it seems to at least indicate at the top corner of it that it was faxed at 3.40 --

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the question is whether the fax actually arrived. There were not that many that worked properly where we were, at least not in time. The phone worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, all right. Well, somehow, when I look at this fax, it seems to me that there's a meeting of the minds between Sarajevo, Tuzla, and Srebrenica because when you look at the next page, which is the document that I've shown you earlier, which was generated by your commander, okay, he says: "I have been ordered by HQ UNPROFOR Sarajevo." And HQ UNPROFOR Sarajevo are the folks that have sent this fax or called or whatever. But this is a document that we received.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Could have been in the evening following the first meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, why don't we take a look at the video, because maybe the video will help us where we can see and hear Lieutenant Karremans himself. And Your Honour, I queued it up. It will take about 2 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Maybe 2 minutes after that, and I'll be through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's passed 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you do it tomorrow afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I certainly can, Your Honour. And I will be through with the witness tomorrow, I would say, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I hope that, you know, after this sitting you could discuss with the court deputy about the numbering of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And before we start tomorrow afternoon, we hope we could receive a list of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. We will do -- well, we will do more than our best to comply with the order, although you must understand I have a rowing boat versus an armada on the other side. So we're rowing as hard as we can, and we're trying our best, but we will endeavour to comply with the Court's wishes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, drawing up a list does not need an armada. We'll resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 7.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of July, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
